subject: Clarify: US addendum - service provider telemetry & cache exclusions (Bluecrest)
messages:
From: Amelia Ford <amelia.ford@bluecrestretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@bluecrestretail.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on US addendum - telemetry caching & service provider language

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending over the US privacy addendum. Our legal team did an initial read and we have two operational clarifications before we can sign:

1) Telemetry caching: the addendum references telemetry retention and a carve-out for transient caching used to improve inference latency. Can you confirm whether Redwood considers prefix/KV cache entries as "telemetry" for the purpose of CCPA/CPRA treatment? If so, what retention window do you advise operationally?

2) Service provider vs processor language: Bluecrest needs firm assurance that data sent under typical inference requests (prompts + user identifiers) is not used for model training or product improvement by Redwood without an opt-in. There is a paragraph in the addendum that suggests limited use for "service improvement" - would you accept a redline that forbids training/derivative-model usage and limits internal troubleshooting access?

We attached our suggested exhibit to show telemetry types we expect to be excluded from "sale" and a short matrix of subprocessors we track. Can you review and confirm by end of week? We are targeting Q1 go-live for the pilot.

Appreciate your help — Amelia

Attachment: bluecrest-telemetry-exhibit.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: subprocessor-matrix-202602.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ford <amelia.ford@bluecrestretail.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on US addendum - telemetry caching & service provider language

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear list and the exhibits, helpful context. Looping in Grace (privacy/legal ops) and Marissa (platform) to confirm specifics. Quick summary from our side: 

- Prefix/KV cache: We treat transient KV/prefix caches as operational telemetry for latency optimization, not as behavioral telemetry or analytics. By default we keep KV cache entries in-memory for the duration of the session plus a short LRU window; typical retention is sub-minute to a few minutes depending on model and request pattern. We can add an explicit contractual definition to the addendum that excludes these ephemeral entries from CCPA "service provider" telemetry that would be considered a "sale."

- Training/product improvement: Redwood’s hosted offering does not train or fine-tune models on customer prompt/content unless a customer opts into an improvement program. We can accept a redline that prohibits use of customer prompts or model outputs for training, model improvement, or derivative model generation. We would, however, ask for a narrow troubleshooting carve-out that allows redacted snapshots for incident investigations (access controls + audit logs).

Grace/Marissa — can you confirm whether those concessions require any changes to our subprocessors list or platform settings, and whether we should add a short example list to the addendum clarifying "transient cache" vs "telemetry logs."

Thanks,
Jordan

Signature:
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on US addendum - telemetry caching & service provider language

Jordan — quick legal ops note. We can accept Bluecrest's redline forbidding training/derivative usage. Required additions to the addendum: 

- Define "Transient inference cache" as data stored solely to serve an in-flight or immediate subsequent request (examples: KV cache, prefix cache) and specify max retention 'operational default' (we'll propose 5 minutes) unless customer-specific setting requested.
- Add explicit prohibition: "Redwood will not use Customer Content for model training, building derivative models, or improving model weights absent express written opt-in."
- Troubleshooting carve-out: allow access to redacted snapshots for severity >=P2 incidents limited to named roles, logged in audit trails, and purged within 30 days.

I'll prepare a short exhibit to attach that lists telemetry classes (cache, request logs, aggregated metrics) and labeling guidance. Marissa — is 5 minutes a safe default on Dedicated/Hosted? Are there any orchestration cases where retention could be longer (e.g., warm pools, autoscaling)?

Grace

Signature:
Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on US addendum - telemetry caching & service provider language

Grace / Jordan — implementation note from infra:

- For Hosted we can commit to an operational default retention of 5 minutes for prefix/KV caches; most inference requests will see much shorter TTLs. We do maintain bounded warm-pool state for throughput (model weights cached on GPU) but that is separate and does not contain customer prompt content.
- For Dedicated customers we can surface a config toggle to reduce cache TTL to near-zero if Bluecrest wants stricter behavior; that would be a per-customer flag and could impact tail latency for bursty workloads.
- Autoscaling: during scale events we may persist some ephemeral request metadata in transient queues for <1 hour to orchestrate safe retries; we can document that as an exception under "orchestration telemetry" and ensure we mark it as not used for analytics/training.

I'll add these specifics to the exhibit and flag the orchestration exception for Grace to review.

Marissa

Signature:
Marissa Cole
Principal, Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Ford <amelia.ford@bluecrestretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@bluecrestretail.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on US addendum - telemetry caching & service provider language

Jordan / Grace / Marissa — thank you for the rapid turnaround and the concrete exhibit language. Bluecrest legal reviewed your proposed definitions and redlines. They are comfortable with: 

- "Transient inference cache" defined with an operational default of 5 minutes; Bluecrest asks that any deviation above 5 minutes be subject to prior written notice.
- Explicit prohibition on using customer content for training/derivative models absent written opt-in.
- Troubleshooting carve-out limited to severity >=P2 incidents, redaction requirement, named roles, and deletion after 30 days.

They have one small ask: please add a short clause that Redwood will provide a quarterly artifact listing active subprocessors and any changes at least 30 days prior to onboarding. That helps our security/compliance team for periodic audits.

If you can incorporate that clause and return a clean PDF, we can route for signature next week and proceed with the Q1 pilot.

Best,
Amelia

Attachment: redlines_us-addendum.docx (docx)
